meta.name: UMC-750 5-Axis Machining Center
meta.summary: 5-axis universal machining center: X/Y/Z 30 × 20 × 20 in, trunnion table with B tilt −35° to +110° and continuous C rotation, 40-taper inline spindle, side-mount tool changer, integrated 75 gal coolant tank. Built from Haas published manuals; alarm numbers beyond the confirmed few are left for the machine's own alarm screen. 3D model drawn to the published overall size, platter and travels; internal layout approximate.

components.name: Base casting
components.desc: Cast-iron base carrying the linear guides; the coolant tank is integrated into it.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: Integrated coolant tank and pumps
components.desc: 75 gal (284 L) tank in the base. Standard and TSC coolant pumps sit on the tool changer side behind the chip conveyor, with a gate filter, coolant box filter and chip tray.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: Trunnion (B axis)
components.desc: Tilting trunnion: B axis from −35° to +110°. Carries the C-axis platter; has its own rotary brake.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

parts.name: Rotary oil fill and drain plug

components.name: C-axis platter (table)
components.desc: 500 × 630 mm table with 7 × 16 mm T-slots on 63 mm centers, continuous 360° C rotation. Max 300 kg evenly distributed. Drawn as Ø500 mm with 7 T-slots on 63 mm centres.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: B-axis rotary drive
components.desc: Servomotor and gear train driving the trunnion tilt, with brake and rotary oil.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: C-axis rotary drive
components.desc: Servomotor and gear train under the platter for C rotation, with brake.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: Column and Y saddle
components.desc: Carries the X and Y linear guides and ballscrews that move the spindle head.
components.src: estimated layout

components.name: X-axis servo motor and ballscrew
components.desc: X travel 762 mm. Motor, coupling, ballscrew and support bearings.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: Y-axis servo motor and ballscrew
components.desc: Y travel 508 mm.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: Z-axis servo motor and ballscrew
components.desc: Z travel 508 mm; spindle nose 102–610 mm from the table.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: Spindle head
components.desc: Moves in Z; holds the spindle cartridge, motor, drawbar unclamp and air regulator.
components.src: estimated layout

components.name: Spindle cartridge (40-taper)
components.desc: Inline direct-drive 40-taper spindle (8,100 rpm standard, 12,000/15,000 optional). Drawbar, disc springs and tool unclamp.
components.src: published UMC-750 specs

components.name: Side-mount tool changer (40+1)
components.desc: Side-mount tool changer with double arm, cam box and carousel; chips build up here weekly.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: Enclosure
components.desc: Full sheet-metal enclosure with safety windows. Overall 4,267 × 2,350 × 2,794 mm with the chip conveyor.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: Operator doors and interlock
components.desc: Doors with an interlock; with the door open and the setup keyswitch locked, operations stop.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: Control pendant (NGC)
components.desc: Next Generation Control pendant: screen, keyboard, E-stop, cycle start, feed hold, handle jog, setup keyswitch.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: Electrical cabinet
components.desc: Control processor, I/O, vector drive, servo amplifiers, power supplies, regen resistor and fans.
components.src: Haas Factory Outlet preventive maintenance checklist

components.name: Chip conveyor
components.desc: Carries chips out on the tool changer side, over the coolant pumps.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: Axis grease and lube unit
components.desc: Automatic axis lubrication; check reservoir level monthly.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: Air regulator panel
components.desc: Shop air in: 4 scfm at 100 psi (113 L/min at 6.9 bar). Feeds spindle air, tool unclamp and the tool changer.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

components.name: WIPS probe and tool setter
components.desc: Wireless probing: work probe in the spindle and tool setter on the table. Used to check MRZP offsets.
components.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

faults.title: Servos off
causes: E-stop pressed, or the machine just powered up
Door or interlock fault holding the servos off
Servo power not restored after an alarm
checks: Release every E-stop, press RESET and POWER UP / zero return
Clear any other active alarm first; it is often the real cause
Check the door interlock if the alarm returns when the door closes
faults.src: Haas NGC alarm search (alarm 102 exists on NGC)

faults.title: Servo error too large
causes: Axis blocked: crash, chips under the way covers, fixture against a guard
Axis binding from dry ways or a damaged ballscrew or coupling
Servo motor, encoder cable or amplifier fault
Control processor fault (rare)
checks: Note which axis, the program line and any damage before resetting
Jog the axis slowly at low rapid override and watch for hesitation
Check way covers, lube and the motor-to-ballscrew coupling
Swap encoder cables or amplifiers between axes to isolate
Back up parameters before replacing boards
faults.src: Haas NGC alarm search; diagnosis per published case notes

faults.title: Emergency off
causes: E-stop button pressed on the pendant or an external E-stop
Open E-stop circuit wiring
checks: Release the E-stop and reset
If no button is pressed, check the E-stop circuit and any external stops wired to the machine
faults.src: Haas NGC alarm search (alarm 107 exists on NGC)

faults.title: Axis servo overload or overheat
causes: Heavy cut or rapid duty beyond the axis rating
Binding or dry ways
Rotary brake not fully released (B/C)
checks: Check the axis load meter during the cycle
Check lubrication and the way covers
For B/C, listen for the brake releasing and check rotary air pressure
faults.src: general 5-axis machining-center practice — confirm the alarm number and text in Haas alarm search

faults.title: B or C axis won't move / brake fault
causes: Rotary brake air or solenoid fault
Low shop air
Brake worn or contaminated
checks: Check air at the regulator (100 psi supply)
Command the brake on and off from the diagnostics page and listen for the solenoid
Inspect the rotary for coolant intrusion
faults.src: general 5-axis machining-center practice — confirm the alarm number and text in Haas alarm search

faults.title: 5-axis features out of position after tilting
causes: Machine Rotary Zero Point (MRZP) offsets drifted
Wrong B or C work offset used with DWO (G254)
Rotary backlash or a crash moved the trunnion
checks: Check the MRZP offsets with WIPS (Operator's Manual Supplement ch. 4)
Do not use a B-axis work offset in programs that use G254 DWO
Check rotary backlash with an indicator
faults.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

faults.title: C axis unwinds through many turns on zero return
causes: C-axis rotary unwind setting off, so the axis returns through the full accumulated rotation
checks: Enable C-axis rotary unwind per the supplement (ch. 8)
Check setting 247 for simultaneous XYZ motion during tool change
faults.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

faults.title: Spindle overload
causes: Cut too heavy, or a dull tool
Spindle bearing damage
Spindle drive fault
checks: Watch the spindle load meter during the cut
Inspect the tool
Turn the spindle by hand (power off) and feel for roughness
Check the vector drive alarm history
faults.src: general 5-axis machining-center practice — confirm the alarm number and text in Haas alarm search

faults.title: Spindle orientation fault
causes: Orientation sensor or encoder fault
Mechanical slip between motor and spindle
checks: Check the orientation position against the tool changer arm
Inspect the sensor and its cable
Re-set the orientation offset only per Haas procedure
faults.src: general 5-axis machining-center practice — confirm the alarm number and text in Haas alarm search

faults.title: Tool won't release or clamp
causes: Low air pressure to the unclamp cylinder
Clamp or unclamp switch misadjusted
Weak or broken disc springs (low drawbar force)
Dirty taper or pull stud
checks: Check the spindle air regulator pressure
Watch the clamp and unclamp inputs on the diagnostics page
Measure drawbar force (yearly check)
Clean and lightly lubricate the taper
faults.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G; Haas Factory Outlet preventive maintenance checklist

faults.title: Tool changer arm or carousel fault
causes: Chips in the carousel or pockets
Cam box motor or position switch fault
Arm plunger or adjuster worn
Low air for pocket up/down
checks: Clear chips from the tool changer (weekly task)
Use the tool changer recovery on the control
Inspect the arm plunger and adjuster (6-month task)
Check the cam box and carousel belts
faults.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G; Haas Factory Outlet preventive maintenance checklist

faults.title: Coolant level low or no coolant flow
causes: Coolant consumed or leaking
Gate or box filter blocked
Pump failed or air-locked
checks: Check level and concentration (weekly)
Clean the coolant filters
Check the pump runs and the TSC pressure
faults.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

faults.title: Axis lubrication low
causes: Grease reservoir empty
Lube line broken
checks: Check the reservoir level (monthly)
Inspect lube hoses for cracking (6-month task)
faults.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

faults.title: Low air pressure
causes: Shop air below 100 psi or under 4 scfm
Regulator filter blocked
Air leak at the spindle, tool changer or rotary brakes
checks: Read the regulator gauge with the machine idle and during a tool change
Drain and service the filter
Listen for leaks
faults.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

faults.title: Door open / interlock
causes: Door opened during automatic operation
Interlock switch misaligned
checks: Close the door and reset
Check the interlock daily as the manual requires
Use the setup keyswitch only for setup; with it locked and the door open, motion stops
faults.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

faults.title: Electrical cabinet or vector drive overheating
causes: Vector drive vents or filter clogged
Cabinet fan failed
checks: Clean the vector drive air vents and filter (monthly)
Check that the cabinet fans run
Inspect the regen resistor
faults.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G; Haas Factory Outlet preventive maintenance checklist
faults.safety: Lock out the main disconnect and wait for the drive DC bus to discharge before opening the cabinet.

faults.title: Probe not responding
causes: WIPS probe or tool setter battery low
Probe not switched on or out of range of the receiver
checks: Replace the probe batteries
Check the receiver and its window are clean
Recalibrate probing after any crash
faults.src: Haas Factory Outlet preventive maintenance checklist

sequence.name: Power up and zero return
sequence.desc: Main disconnect on, control boots, E-stop reset, servos on, then zero return for X, Y, Z, B and C.

sequence.name: Spindle and axis warm-up
sequence.desc: Run the warm-up program before precision 5-axis work to stabilize the spindle and axes thermally.

sequence.name: Tool change (M06)
sequence.desc: Spindle orients, Z moves to tool change height, the double arm swaps tools, the drawbar unclamps and reclamps.

sequence.name: Work setup and probing
sequence.desc: Probe the part with WIPS to set work offsets; check MRZP offsets periodically.

sequence.name: 5-axis cutting
sequence.desc: Simultaneous X, Y, Z, B and C motion with tool center point control (G234) or dynamic work offset (G254); flood or through-spindle coolant on.

sequence.name: End of cycle
sequence.desc: Spindle stops, coolant off, axes return, C axis unwinds if set.

checks.name: Daily checks
checks.why: Safety items the manual requires every shift.
steps: Inspect the enclosure windows for damage
Check the door interlock works
Check coolant level
checks.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

checks.name: Weekly checks
checks.why: Chips and coolant condition cause most tool changer and finish problems.
steps: Clean chips out of the tool changer
Check coolant concentration with a refractometer
Check spindle air regulator pressure
checks.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

checks.name: Monthly checks
checks.why: Keeps axes lubricated and drives cool.
steps: Check the axis grease reservoir level
Clean the vector drive air vents and filter
Inspect and lubricate the way covers
checks.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

checks.name: Every six months
steps: Completely clean the coolant tank and replace the coolant
Clean the standard coolant filter
Check the coolant refill works
Inspect the oil skimmer pickup tube
Inspect auxiliary filter and axis lube hoses for cracking
Inspect the tool changer arm plunger and adjuster assembly
checks.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

checks.name: Yearly checks
checks.why: Wear items on the tool changer, spindle and rotary.
steps: Grease the tool changer cams
Clean the MQL reservoir filter (if fitted)
Inspect the rotary axis oil
Check drawbar force
checks.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G; MaintainX UMC-750 PM list

checks.name: Rotary oil change
checks.why: Gear oil in the trunnion breaks down and picks up contamination.
steps: Replace rotary axis oil every 2 years (or per the Haas rotary service manual)
Inspect for coolant in the oil when it is drained

checks.name: MRZP check
checks.why: 5-axis accuracy depends on the machine knowing where the rotary centers are.
steps: Check MRZP offsets with WIPS per supplement ch. 4
Record parameter 1314 and set it to 0 during the check, as the procedure says
Only change parameters with Haas factory instructions
checks.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-0202 rev E

checks.name: Service-level PM (HFO checklist)
checks.why: Deeper checks done by a technician.
steps: Megger spindle and axis motors
Check backlash on all axes and machine level
Inspect and ohm the regen resistor
Check AC, high-voltage DC and low-voltage DC power
Check the processor battery and probe batteries
Check tool changer alignment, tool change height and pushout
checks.src: Haas Factory Outlet preventive maintenance checklist

reference.name: UMC-750 specifications
reference.intro: From the Haas operator's manual supplement.
rows: 500 × 630 mm, 7 T-slots 16 mm on 63 mm centers
40-taper inline direct drive, 8,100 rpm (12k/15k optional), 30 hp
4 scfm at 100 psi (113 L/min at 6.9 bar)
notes: Spindle, rpm, hp and tool changer figures are from dealer listings of the published spec; check the machine's options.

reference.name: 5-axis functions
reference.intro: Control features the UMC relies on.
rows: Tool center point control: keeps the tool tip on path while B/C move
Dynamic work offset: work offset follows the rotary position
Machine rotary zero point: where the B/C axes cross; stored in parameters 1306–1308
Simultaneous XYZ motion during tool change
notes: Don't use a B-axis work offset with G254.

reference.name: Looking up alarms
reference.intro: Haas publishes every alarm with causes and checks online.
rows: Same number with the axis identified in the alarm text
Note the alarm, program line and any damage; save an error report
notes: This profile uses the alarm numbers that could be confirmed (102, 103, 107); the rest are listed by symptom. Add numbers from your machine's alarm history.

devices.func: Switches power to the drives when servos are on
NGC main processor; processor battery checked at service PM
Machine inputs and outputs: door, air, lube, coolant, tool changer sensors and solenoids
Spindle drive and DC bus supply; air vents/filter cleaned monthly
Rotary B and C servo amplifiers
Absorbs braking energy from the spindle and axes; inspect and ohm at PM
Low-voltage DC supplies for the control and I/O
Emergency stop and door interlock circuit

defects.name: Features shift between 3+2 setups
defects.looks: Features cut at different B/C angles don't line up; steps or mismatches between faces.
isolate: Cut a test part with features at several B/C angles and measure

causes.fix: Recheck and update MRZP per the Haas procedure

causes.cause: Rotary backlash or brake not holding during cut
causes.fix: Check backlash; check rotary brake air

causes.cause: B-axis work offset used with G254
causes.fix: Remove B offset when using DWO

defects.src: Haas UMC-750 Operator's Manual Supplement 96-8250 rev G

defects.name: Gouging during simultaneous 5-axis moves
defects.looks: Unexpected cuts or marks on finished faces during tilted moves.
isolate: Run the program in graphics or dry-run with the part removed
Check TCPC is active where the CAM expects it

causes.fix: Use the Haas UMC post and correct machine data

causes.cause: Tool length offset wrong with TCPC

defects.name: Chatter on tilted features
defects.looks: Chatter where the part is tilted and the tool sticks out further.
isolate: Compare finish at B=0 and at the tilted angle

causes.cause: Long stick-out to reach tilted faces
causes.fix: Use the shortest tool that clears; tilt the part to shorten reach

causes.cause: Weak workholding high above the platter
Rotary brake not clamped for 3+2 cuts
